label-convention-as-convention.statement: Every rule in this domain sits on one of three footings: documented platform behaviour, a published measurement, or practitioner convention. A technique says which, and a generated recommendation says which. The difficulty-below-authority ceiling, the six-of-ten intent count, the subhead interval, the four-field form, the cadence cap - useful habits, all of them, and none a law of the engine. A convention presented as documented behaviour is the domain's most reproduced error and the reason a corpus of marketing advice ages into folklore.

never-invent-proof.statement: No number, review, credential, price, address, contact, guarantee or competitor fact goes on any surface or into any prompt output unless the business supplied it. A missing proof is an open question put to the owner, or an explicitly empty slot - never a plausible value, never a blank left silently, never a disclaimer padding it. In generated output this is enforced structurally: schemas that cannot carry a number, validators that drop entities not in the request, grounding that hands only facts to the model. An instruction alone does not satisfy the law.

not-measured-is-not-zero.statement: A missing denominator, an absent prior window, a metric a platform never reported, a link nobody clicked yet, a channel with no read-back - each is absent, and absence is rendered as absent: null, blank, "not measured", a dropped column. Zero is a verdict, and a fabricated zero seeds every baseline, average and comparison downstream with a lie. The same rule forbids summing money across currencies and blending a predicted score into a measured one.

statistical-honesty-before-a-verdict.statement: Comparison windows are weekday-balanced and equal in length, year-over-year lands on the same weekday, partial buckets are flagged and never compared, ratios of sums carry no confidence claim, an experiment needs its sample before it needs its winner, and the multiple-comparison correction is applied before any arm is declared. A verdict without these is a coin flip with a badge; an honest "not yet measurable" outranks it.

provenance-is-binary-and-labelled.statement: Every number a marketing surface shows is either the business's own synced data or disclosed illustrative data, decided per surface and per request, never blended, and the label sits beside the number rather than in a footer. Illustrative data is never indexed as proof, never diagnosed as if it were the client's, never scored as a track record, and never lets a generated recommendation read as an account win. The disclosure is dropped on the real branch, because a caveat on real data is the opposite lie.

platform-reported-is-not-causal.statement: An ad platform's conversion count is its own attribution of itself, and a before/after read around a change is a description, not an experiment. Last-click credits the channel that closed and starves the channel that prospected; two platforms blended together double-count the same order. Causal claims need a holdout, a geo split or a model that says its own error; everything else is labelled as the descriptive read it is, and a marketer who acts on it says so.

the-results-page-is-the-verdict.statement: Search intent, cluster membership, difficulty and competitor choice are all read off the live results page, never off a tool's label or a modifier word. A tool's intent label is a hint that is wrong often enough to be dangerous; a modifier list is a hint that systematically over-labels queries as informational. When a decision about a keyword is made, somebody has searched it and read what the engine chose to rank. The corollary is that any threshold placed on that reading - six of ten, four shared results - is an internal convention and is labelled as one.

one-target-one-threshold.statement: A business has one agreed performance target per scope, and every badge, cell colour, sort, alert, report line and prompt reads the same one; a derived threshold is the reciprocal of its sibling by construction so two cells cannot disagree about one campaign. Lower-is-better metrics invert the verdict, never the number. When a target has a narrower scope than the whole business - paid portfolio versus blended - every surface labels the scope, so a looser number is never read as a contradiction.

a-gate-before-money-and-copy.statement: Nothing changes spend without simulate, guardrail, explicit approval and a reversible ledger; nothing publishes without the channel confirming it; nothing auto-sends to a customer while a risk is listed, whatever the confidence claims. Audits and fix passes change the mechanical layer only - tags, metadata, markup, links, images - and never the body copy a person approved. Deletion of a page, a keyword map, a listing or a review is a recommendation awaiting a yes, because a deleted URL loses its links and rankings permanently.

efficiency-is-not-profitability.statement: Return on ad spend and its inverse measure spend against revenue, not against profit. Without a margin, a surface speaks of efficiency and refuses to judge profitability; with one, break-even is the inverse of margin, a channel is profitable when its net profit is non-negative rather than when its ratio clears a target, and reallocation ranks by profit destroyed rather than by revenue missed. A zero-cost channel is never a false loss and a high-ratio low-margin channel is never a false win.
